items.checks: Read the actual translated set, star projection and every nearest-point/uniqueness argument. Closed L supplies completeness, and the actual projection formula gives linearity iff p is in L iff zero belongs to the affine set; no nearest-point certificate is assumed.

The rebase equality and translate inclusion iff subspace inclusion justify a common point of the nested nonempty affine spaces. Both absorption orders and the exact squared-norm Pythagoras identity use the actual subspace orthogonality.

Read the whole finite list product proof and its Fin n specialization. It identifies the actual range with the full intersection, identifies the selfadjoint idempotent with its actual metric projection, proves every permutation and covers the empty list. The reverse two-factor implication uses selfadjointness, not idempotence alone.

Read both complete reused modules. The minimizers are constructed by the actual Hilbert projection theorem. Uniform finite feasibility bounds the finite energy supremum, and the entire Finset I directed net is proved Cauchy without a cofinal sequence. Completeness, all individual closed constraints, actual minimum, exact energy supremum and nonexpansiveness are proved, including empty I.

The singleton nonnegative ray satisfies every finite feasibility condition with B=0. The max function is proved to equal the same global_project used in S4, and its midpoint failure is explicit on the full real domain.

Read the VI equivalence and full contraction construction. The norm estimate uses the supplied strong monotonicity and Lipschitz bounds; the projection is only used as nonexpansive. Banach yields existence and uniqueness, with every initial point and iterate in the geometric bound. The sqrt convention plus s<=sqrt(s)^2 correctly handles the zero Hilbert space and q=0, without an unjustified m<=L assumption.
